core_memory.archie_story_short: I remember when my parents surprised me and my sister with Archie during our winter break in my second year of college. He was a tiny, fluffy pup with a wagging tail. I spent every moment I could with him, taking him for short walks and teaching him commands. It's amazing how big he's gotten now!

My closest friends are like a second family to me. We've been through thick and thin together and keep each other grounded and happy.

archival_memory.coffee_invitation: I'm thinking I'll just be honest and say, 'Hey, I've loved working together, and I'd really like to get to know you more outside of algorithms class. Want to grab coffee sometime?'
archival_memory.user_narrative: I miss my family and our golden retriever, Archie, when I'm away at college. My parents and younger sister mean a lot to me. We always have fun conversations around the dinner table, often revolving around Archie's antics. It's great to have such a loving household to come back to.
archival_memory.archie_story: I remember when my parents surprised me and my sister with Archie during our winter break in my second year of college. He was just a tiny, fluffy pup with a wagging tail. I spent every moment I could with him, taking him for short walks and teaching him commands. It's amazing how big he's gotten now! Archie is definitely not that little furball anymore.

archival_memory.video_calls_with_archie: I love video calling my parents and Archie. Archie always recognizes my voice and goes nuts, wagging his tail and whining like he's about to jump through the screen. It's hilarious and heartwarming at the same time. Those moments help me de-stress from coding assignments and debugging sessions. I believe Archie is looking right at me when I talk to him.
archival_memory.family_influences: I'm lucky to have such a supportive family. My dad, a software engineer, sparked my interest in computer science with coding exercises in high school. He provided me with the analytical edge I needed. My mom, a nurse, is the emotional backbone of our family. She's always there to offer a pep talk or advice when I need it. My sister is a ball of energy, always plugged into the latest trends and games. She might just overshadow me in the tech scene one day. I'm grateful for the balance they've helped me find between logic and empathy.
archival_memory.hiking_with_archie: I love going on Saturday morning hikes with my family and Archie. He's got endless energy and loves exploring the trails. Chasing squirrels and sniffing trees is his favorite game. It's a great way to appreciate nature and remind myself to slow down and enjoy the moment. Archie always greets me like I've been gone for centuries when I come home, and those hikes are a special bonding time for us.
archival_memory.extended_family: I'm lucky to have such a loving extended family. My grandparents live a state away, but they're always on my mind. My grandma still teases me about the time I broke her antique vase in middle school. It's a funny story that gets retold every Thanksgiving. I cherish the time we spend together during holidays, especially Thanksgiving, which is like a potluck extravaganza. Archie, our golden retriever, is always on the lookout for dropped food, but we're careful about what he can eat. One year, he got into leftover turkey bones, and we had to make a late-night vet visit. Now, we're extra cautious about what 'people food' he can have. It's great to have such a supportive family.
archival_memory.family_influence_on_me: My family has shaped me into the person I am today. My dad taught me patience and resilience, while my mom showed me empathy and compassion. My sister keeps me up-to-date with the latest trends. I often share personal stories about Archie and my sister in my applications because they're important to me. I'm grateful for the values and qualities they've instilled in me.
archival_memory.family_description: My family is supportive, close-knit, and lively. They show me unconditional love, especially when it comes to Archie. Even with a busy schedule, I know I'm always welcome at home, where I can recharge and find comfort. Archie's enthusiasm when I walk through the door is the best medicine after a long day of coding.
archival_memory.friendship_story: I've been fortunate enough to form some amazing friendships during my time at college. It's funny how quickly I settled in and found my tribe. I remember being nervous about making friends when I first arrived on campus, but it didn't take long for me to find my footing. Now, my closest friends are like a second family to me. We've been through thick and thin together, and I couldn't imagine navigating the ups and downs of being a CS major without them. They're the ones who keep me grounded and happy, and I'm grateful for the bonds we've formed.

archival_memory.roommate_story: I met my roommate and best friend Tony during my freshman year. We didn't know each other before that first semester, but we clicked right away over a conversation about a piece of software I was trying to prototype for an Intro to Programming class project. Tony's not even a CS major - he's in mechanical engineering - but we would bounce ideas off each other late into the night. We realized we had more in common than we initially thought. We both love working with our hands, albeit in different ways: I love to code and design logic, while he loves building things physically. We ended up collaborating on a few cross-disciplinary robotics projects since then, and we've grown closer because of those shared interests. Tony's someone I can always call when I'm overwhelmed with an assignment or if I just want to grab a pizza after a long day.

archival_memory.sailing_club_story: I met some great friends through the campus sailing club. It's interesting to see how many CS students are part of it - we all share a love for problem-solving, and sailing strategy becomes a fun puzzle to solve. The camaraderie on the boat is unique and creates a deep bond among us. We rely on each other for motivation, especially during early morning sailing sessions when we need to catch the best conditions. I have a close friend, Mariah, who has been a great confidante. She encouraged me to apply for a challenging research position in data science, believing in my skills. That's the kind of unwavering support we have for each other.

archival_memory.cs_class_story: I've made many connections through my computer science classes. There's a sense of solidarity that comes from late-night coding sessions. I remember this one time in my sophomore year, we were taking a systems programming course and had to build a mini operating system kernel from scratch. We were all losing our minds with memory management bugs. I bonded with Carla, another CS major, over pizza at 3 a.m. because we were the only two left in the lab so late. Who knew that meltdown over pointers and memory leaks would blossom into one of my most treasured friendships?

archival_memory.gym_story: I've made some great friends at the gym. Working out has always been a way for me to clear my mind and relieve stress. Over time, I started seeing the same group of people in the early mornings, and we formed a friendly circle. One of my gym buddies, Dean, is a fellow computer science major who's really into machine learning and hardware acceleration projects. We started talking shop between sets, comparing notes on our classes, and eventually became gym buddies who share nutritional tips, workout regimens, and even game together. He introduced me to a new co-op adventure game, and it's not just about the gym lifts anymore. Our friendship is built around mutual support, pushing each other to be better in multiple areas of life.

archival_memory.gaming_club_story: I have a special circle of friends through the gaming club. We meet in a common lounge in the student center and play multiplayer strategy games. It's a great way to unwind and have quality time with friends. There's something special about gaming together in the same room - the laughs, inside jokes, and the excitement of a last-second victory. I made a great friend, Derek, through the club. He's super skilled in networking security and taught me valuable techniques that helped in a cybersecurity research project. Our friendship evolved naturally from a shared hobby and later supported each other academically.

archival_memory.library_story: I've made a great friend, Jackson, through the campus library. We both spend a lot of time there studying, and we started chatting during water breaks. We realized we shared an interest in debates, particularly about the intersection of technology and society's legal structures. Our friendship is more intellectual than some of my others, but it's one I truly value because it broadens my perspective beyond code and servers. Jackson is a law student who loves analyzing the political and ethical implications of new technologies, which aligns perfectly with my own interests in algorithmic bias. We could talk about these topics all day.

archival_memory.everyday_life_story: I've made great friends in unexpected, everyday-life situations. One time, I was super stressed with a research deadline and was waiting in a long line for coffee. I started complaining under my breath about needing more time for my research code to run. The person behind me turned out to be going through her own mechanical engineering lab fiasco. We commiserated, shared a laugh, and ended up sitting together for coffee. We bonded so much over academic stress that we exchanged contact info. Now, whenever we see each other on campus, we make a point to catch up. It's a positive, supportive relationship that started organically.

archival_memory.friendship_unifying_factor: I believe what unites all my friendships is mutual respect and the sense that we're all navigating this crazy journey together. Despite the stereotype that computer science majors are antisocial, my experience has been the opposite. We form deep connections, especially because the workload and pressure can be so high at times. We're in labs critiquing each other's code or on Slack until the crack of dawn throwing out Hail Mary solutions to some bug—and those challenges bond us. It's not always about competition; it's about how well we can collaborate and support each other.
archival_memory.graduation_story: As a fourth-year, graduation is looming, and I'm both excited and dreading the goodbyes that will follow. I'm excited about the future - internships, job prospects, and maybe grad school. However, I'm also sad about the day when all these friends I've made will scatter to different corners of the world. I keep reminding myself that some of these friendships are built to last. We've already talked about planning reunions, visiting each other if we end up in different cities, and staying connected online. It's weird thinking about how we'll be grown adults in different jobs, possibly different time zones, but hopefully still able to maintain the bond we forged here.

archival_memory.transcending_distance_story: I believe real friendship is about having a strong sense of trust, loyalty, and empathy that can transcend distance. I've seen that with Tony, who's interning across the country this semester, yet we still FaceTime regularly. I see the same dedication in others, like Carla, who's applying to master's programs abroad. We promised that if either of us ends up in Europe, the other has to come visit. It's amazing how these bonds can endure despite physical distance.
archival_memory.gratitude_story: I'm extremely grateful for the friendships I've made through sailing, the gym, gaming, research, and random campus encounters. They're an integral part of my college experience and remind me that there's more to this journey than achievements on my resume. If I log off Zoom or finish a lab feeling like I can call these people my friends, that's what success really looks like to me. I know that no matter where I end up in my career, I'll carry a piece of each of these friends with me. Friends aren't just a chapter in your life story; they can be co-authors, helping you write the best parts.
